title: Plugins that register themselves
description:
Build a tiny plugin system with an abstract base class.

- `Exporter` is an `ABC` with an abstract method `export(rows)` that returns a string. `rows` is a list of dictionaries with the same keys.
- Each subclass gives a format name when it is declared: `class CsvExporter(Exporter, fmt="csv")`. `__init_subclass__` stores the class in `Exporter.formats` under that name. Declaring a second class with a name already used raises `ValueError`.
- `CsvExporter` produces a header line of the keys (in the order of the first row) and one line per row, values joined by commas, each line ending in `\n`. No rows gives an empty string.
- `MarkdownExporter` (`fmt="md"`) produces a table: `| a | b |`, then `|---|---|`, then a line per row, each ending in `\n`. No rows gives an empty string.
- `export_as(fmt, rows)` creates the right exporter and calls it; an unknown format raises `KeyError`.

```python
rows = [{"name": "Ada", "age": 36}, {"name": "Alan", "age": 41}]
print(export_as("csv", rows), end="")
# name,age
# Ada,36
# Alan,41
```
hints: `def __init_subclass__(cls, fmt, **kwargs):` receives the `fmt=` from the class line. Call `super().__init_subclass__(**kwargs)` first, then check and store `cls`.
`list(rows[0])` gives the keys of the first row in order. `",".join(str(row[k]) for k in keys)` makes one CSV line.
